releases.title: Vertical Pong and Power Battle

new: Play Pong on a vertical court with yourself always defending from the bottom, including in student battles.
Collect seven temporary boosts, use Forward Rush, and choose Power Battle for explicitly accepted student matches.
improved: Paddle movement and impact position now shape capped ball speed, angle and spin, with motion-aware visual effects and optional sound.
The deterministic computer opponent can collect boosts and adapt within each level's limits.

reviewEvidence: Reviewed the scoped frontend and backend changes and their Pong UI, physics and school-isolation tests.
Local checks passed: 204 backend tests, 216 Flutter tests, 13 focused Pong widget tests, 29 focused physics tests, Flutter analysis and release web build.

Authenticated two-client browser QA verified mirrored bottom-player views, accepted Power Battle, paddle-collected Wide Paddle, synchronized 7-5 finish and teacher Power Battle disable while Classic remained available.
Release validation will rerun full suites and build from clean committed archives before deployment.

releases.title: Pong Challenge

new: Play Pong against the computer across 15 levels with saved progress and replay.
Invite an available student in your school to a fair first-to-seven Pong battle.
Teachers and management can enable games, computer play and student battles for each learner.
improved: Pong supports keyboard, drag and touch controls, with calm visuals and reduced motion.
Games pause on connection loss and preserve saved progress when access changes.

reviewEvidence: Reviewed paired source diffs, additive default-off profile migration, school-scoped models, server-authoritative physics and result transactions.
192 backend tests passed without skips, including all 15 levels, cross-school isolation, invitation races, reconnect and unchanged academic XP.
212 Flutter tests passed; flutter analyze reported no issues; release web build passed.

Local browser QA with synthetic teacher and two students verified default-off access, teacher enable/disable, Level 1 completion and Level 2 unlock, persisted stats, private lobby, invitation acceptance, matching 7-6 result on both clients, consented rematch, solo pause/resume and arena return navigation.
Production smoke will use explicitly authorized dedicated test accounts, followed by account archival.

releases.title: Clearer release notes

fixed: Made release-note headings easier to read.

reviewEvidence: Reviewed the exact diff since deployed/v2.1.0: the release-history headings now use the dialog foreground color rather than the white button label style. Existing widget tests now use the real application theme and assert at least 4.5:1 heading contrast. No business logic or backend source changed.

releases.title: Mission creation and version history

new: Open the version button to see what changed and browse previous releases.
A New indicator highlights updates you have not viewed yet.
improved: Production updates now receive a consistent version and release notes before publication.
fixed: Fixed an issue that could prevent teachers from creating missions after uploading lesson material.
Existing accounts keep their school context when signing in or restoring a session.

reviewEvidence: Compared the last verified paired production release (2.0.0) with both current Git revisions, reviewed the actual middleware, account resolution, session serialization and tests; production read-only audit confirmed all 36 accounts already have the current school.

The schoolBoundMiddleware captures trusted AsyncLocalStorage before Multer and restores it on completion/error. All teacher/student upload routes use it. Existing scoped query and reference validation remain in force; database regressions cover all mission formats and reject cross-school operations.
Legacy backfill uses a persisted pre-migration identity and exactly one school including inactive schools; new unassigned accounts and multi-school ambiguity reject rather than guess.
ReleaseHistoryButton uses canonical generated data with account-specific local viewing preferences. Widget tests preserve old history, separate accounts and check 320px enlarged-text layout.

Release tooling binds reviewed notes to both source digests, chooses semantic versions, validates clean Git archives, protects tags/history and checks exact provider revision plus public artifacts. Render startup refuses changed, unvalidated source. No progression, scores, XP, certification, assignments or result business logic changed.
